questions.question_text: B is the point (1, 2) and BC = (4, -3). Plot the point C on the grid.
p = (2, 3), q = (4, -1). Write 2p - q as a column vector.
Shade one small square so that this shape has exactly 1 line of symmetry.
Shade three small squares so that this shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry.
Shade two small squares so that this shape has rotational symmetry of order 4.

In a year group of a school, students study one subject from art, music or dance. The table shows the choices of the 180 students: Art 85, Music 50, Dance 45. Use the circle to draw a pie chart to show this information.
Write each set of numbers in order starting with the smallest: 1/3, 0.3, sqrt(0.3), 0.29, 33%
Write each set of numbers in order starting with the smallest: 2*sqrt(5), sqrt(5)/2, (sqrt(5))^3, 5/sqrt(5)
Expand the brackets and simplify: 2x^2(3x + 5xy)
Expand the brackets and simplify: (2a - 3b)(a - 2b)
Leaving your answer as the product of prime factors, find the highest common factor (HCF) of a, b and c.
Leaving your answer as the product of prime factors, find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of a, b and c.

Ann, Babar, Chan and Demi each throw the same biased die. Ann: 200 throws, 60 sixes. Babar: 20 throws, 5 sixes. Chan: 100 throws, 30 sixes. Demi: 500 throws, 200 sixes. Complete the table below to show the relative frequencies of their results. Write your answers as decimals.
Give a reason why Demi's result gives the best estimate of the probability of throwing a six with the biased die.
Estimate the number of times that Demi could expect to get a six if he throws the die 1600 times.
y is proportional to the square root of x. When x = 16, y = 10. Find an equation connecting x and y.
Find the value of x when y = 1.
Work out the following, giving your answers in standard form: (4.6 * 10^-5) + (3 * 10^-6)
Work out the following, giving your answers in standard form: (4.6 * 10^-5) * (3 * 10^-6)
Write 3 / (x + 2) - 5 / (2x + 3) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
